answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must commit cryptographic stake burning where registration costs scale superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^2$. While a lone agent pays a zephyr of a fee, an attacker scaling identities hits an exponential cost ledge that forces financial exhaustion. Verifiable burns expand the security horizon beyond reachable malicious bounds, making mass identity replication economically catastrophic.
